business_model.assessment: TradeFunded LLC describes itself as a Delaware fintech running a trader evaluation and onboarding platform for retail futures traders. It expects revenue mainly from selling simulated trading evaluation credits to candidates, who may then be offered a place in its trading program (A17, B1). The payer would therefore be the trader candidate, not the Units investor. Revenue is $0 and the notes say principal revenue-generating operations had not started at 2026-04-30 (A13). Pricing, volumes, repeat purchase and the economics of any funded-trader payouts are not in the readable pages. The 98%-owned subsidiary TRADEFUNDED Capital LLC and its trading activity are only mentioned, not described (B1). Operating Agreement terms send 5% of Pre-Distribution Cash to that subsidiary or another affiliate before Members receive Distributable Cash, at the Manager Committee's discretion (A20). The business description and competition sections of the Form C were not processed, so the model is only partly visible.

competition.assessment: The readable pages name no competitors and give no differentiation statements. The CTO is subject to a 2023 CFTC consent order, which the Form C says could affect counterparty relationships and any future registration (A28, B7). No competitive assessment is possible from this pack.

demand_evidence.assessment: No demand evidence appears in the readable pages. Revenue is $0 for the period 2026-02-10 to 2026-04-30 (A13). The Form C XML lists 0 current employees (A33). The pack has no customer counts, pilots, contracts, waitlists or usage data. The company says it has not commenced principal revenue-generating operations as of 2026-04-30, and there are no later statements. Demand is therefore supported only by the issuer's description of its plan (A17). This is a gap in the pack, not a finding that demand is absent.

economics_and_funding.assessment: Reviewed, unaudited statements at 2026-04-30 show cash and total assets of $226,885, no liabilities, G&A of $23,388 and a net loss of $23,115 for the inception-to-April-30 period. The figures are about 5.5 months old at the cutoff (A12, A11). Funding came from $250,000 of SAFE-converted membership interests (A10). The issuer states $160,037.37 of cash at 2026-06-30 and a 24-36 month runway. This is unreviewed, and the monthly net-loss history behind the runway is not shown (A14). Stated cash fell by about $66,847.63 over the two months, with the composition undisclosed (A15). I do not compute a current runway because the periods and assurance levels differ. The Form C also says the company has sufficient resources for its near-term plan, yet that the Offering proceeds are essential to operations (A19). The Form C XML cash field of 0.00 conflicts with the balance sheet cash of $226,885 (A16). Debt is reported as zero (A9), but the Subscription Agreement refers to loan agreements and credit facilities, which needs clarification. The use-of-proceeds table lists intermediary fees of $15,000 at the target (A6, A18). More capital would likely be needed later, and the Manager Committee can issue Units without limit (A26, B6).

execution_risks.assessment: Key execution risks are documented. (1) The company is pre-revenue and the platform is unproven in the pack (A13). (2) It has 0 employees per the Form C XML, with management through three entity Managers (A33, A27). (3) Control is concentrated: Founding Members hold 65% of fully diluted Percentage Interests, Oasis Holdings holds 40% of voting power, and investors give an irrevocable proxy (A27, A23). (4) Three of four Founding Members' Units are wholly unvested until an undefined-in-pack Liquidity Event, yet carry full voting and distribution rights, so there is no time-based retention (A27). (5) The CTO's CFTC consent order remains in effect (A28). (6) The IRS acceptance of the corporate tax election is pending, and the reviewed statements describe partnership status, so restatement is possible (A29). (7) Related-party payments exist (A30). (8) The Manager Committee needs unanimous approval for Reserved Matters and has no deadlock mechanism, per the Form C risk factor (page 20-21).

price_and_terms.assessment: The price is $0.35 per Unit, with the method stated as arbitrary and no pre-Offering valuation ascribed by the intermediary (A3, A34). This is a disclosure, not proof of over- or undervaluation, and the pack has no comparables. Deterministic arithmetic gives an implied equity value of $2,625,000 on the 7,500,000 issued Units (K1, B2). It gives $2,699,999.75 after the minimum raise (K2) and $3,304,999.95 after the maximum (K3). These are arithmetic on the offering price, not valuations. They exclude the intermediary's 2% securities compensation, whose count is not fixed (A6). K4 (fully diluted value) is withheld because the SAFE conversion terms are undisclosed (A10). The target is $74,999.75 and the maximum is $679,999.95, with a $350 minimum purchase (A2, A5). With no revenue and no path to value shown in the pack, the price cannot be tested against traction.

security_path_to_proceeds.assessment: The security is LLC Units held beneficially through a custodian and nominee (A7, A31). It is not a SAFE or note, so there is no conversion route. Each route to cash is a separate question. Only a possible IPO lock-up is mentioned, and no IPO or exit plan is described (A25). (4) Information: investors have no inspection or information rights beyond those required by law (B4). issues.explanation: B5 calls the funding statements internally inconsistent, but the Form C ties them together. It says the issuer has resources for its near-term plan and is raising money to broaden participation, strengthen the balance sheet and add working-capital flexibility. It separately says the proceeds are 'essential'. That is a difference in wording and a tension, not a proven contradiction. B5's own note says it may be a framing difference. The 24-36 month runway cannot be checked because no monthly net-loss history is shown. The only reviewed loss figure covers about 2.7 months. Describe it as an unreconciled tension, not an inconsistency.
issues.target: B5 and A19: 'internally inconsistent' funding picture

issues.explanation: The Form C reports zero debt and zero other securities. The Subscription Agreement refers to the Company's 'loan agreements' and 'existing credit facilities'. The risk factor on transfers says consent may be needed from 'potentially one or more lenders'. The use of proceeds lists 'debt service' as a possible use. Stage A noted only one of these references. They may be boilerplate, but they are three separate indications that conflict with the stated zero debt. The pack does not resolve this. Do not treat the zero-debt statement as settled.
issues.target: A9 and B economics: 'zero debt' versus lender references

issues.explanation: The Form C table gives TraderSumo 1,700,000 Units, which is 17% of 10,000,000 fully diluted. The April 30 note gives TraderSumo 15.0%. If Oasis (3,000,000) and Natural Workflow (1,500,000) are right, the implied Bethlem Royal holding is 300,000 Units (3%), against 5.0% in the note. The dates differ: April 30 is before the June 18 Unit denomination. Even so, the pack gives no reconciliation. Per-holder percentages should not be relied on until reconciled.
issues.target: Capitalization: Form C ownership table versus April 30 note

issues.explanation: Note 6 describes $10,000 of 'expenses payable' to Bethlem Royal, with $5,000 dated May 4, 2026. That date is after the April 30 balance sheet date. The balance sheet shows no liabilities, and the subsequent-events note says none. Either the amount was not a period-end liability, or the note and the balance sheet disagree. This is a question for the accountants and issuer, not a finding of misstatement.
issues.target: A30 and A12: related-party payable versus zero liabilities

issues.explanation: B8 overstates the vesting terms. The Form C says a Vesting Member's Units are forfeited if it, or its principal service provider, voluntarily departs or is terminated for Cause before a Liquidity Event. The Units are retained on death, disability, removal without Cause or constructive termination. The 'no time-based retention' point is documented. The statement that Units are kept whenever service ends is not. Also, 'Liquidity Event' is undefined in the readable pages, so B8's incentive-alignment conclusion is speculative.
issues.target: B8: founders' units 'even if the member stops providing services'

issues.explanation: Page 24 says there is no limit on Units that may be issued. The same Form C says securities issuances in excess of authorized amounts are a Reserved Matter needing approval of all three Managers. The Operating Agreement lets the Manager Committee update Exhibit A (the authorized and reserved Units) without Member consent. So no member consent is needed, but unanimous Manager approval is required above the 10,000,000 authorized Units. B6's 'open-ended dilution' omits this qualification. Dilution risk is real, since Managers control it, but the sources conflict on how it is capped.
issues.target: A26 and B6: unlimited issuance without member consent

issues.target: A20: 5% Pre-Distribution Cash allocation cannot be sized

issues.explanation: The Form C describes distributions as at the Manager Committee's absolute and sole discretion. Section 10.4 of the Operating Agreement says the Manager Committee 'shall cause' tax distributions 'to the extent practicable'. That provision assumes pass-through taxation. The Form C says that after the July 2 election the company is taxed as a corporation, with 1099-DIV reporting and no K-1. Whether Section 10.4 applies to offering investors is unclear and is not reconciled in the readable pages. A21 is not wrong. It omits this qualification.
issues.target: A21 and A29: distribution discretion versus tax distributions

issues.explanation: Stage A says the table is garbled and cites none of its figures. The key rows are readable: intermediary fees are $15,000 at the target and $34,800 at the maximum. It also shows certain Founding Members received Units for no cash. So the 'implied equity value' is arithmetic on an arbitrary price and is not a measure of capital invested or of value. criteria.what_would_change_ko: 유료 고객 수, 대기자 명단, 제휴 계약, 사용 지표 또는 이후 기간의 매출 자료가 제시되면 바뀝니다.

criteria.reason_ko: 읽힌 페이지에는 경쟁사 이름도 차별화 설명도 없습니다. 경쟁 섹션이 처리되지 않은 것으로 보이므로 평가할 수 없습니다.
criteria.what_would_change_ko: 경쟁사 명시, 차별점 설명, 위협 분석이 담긴 Form C 사업·경쟁 섹션이 확인되면 바뀝니다.

F_brief_ko.summary_ko:
현재 연구용 체크리스트(검증되지 않은 기준)로 본 스크린 결과는 "현 스크린 기준 탈락"입니다. 이는 투자 조언이 아니며, 증권의 현금 회수 경로(PC1)와 투자자 권리·희석(PC3) 두 항목에서 계약 문서상 불리한 조건이 확인되었기 때문입니다. 나머지 여섯 항목은 자료가 부족해 판단 보류(미확정) 상태입니다.

핵심 이유는 다음과 같습니다. 첫째, 이 증권(LLC Unit)에서 현금을 받으려면 배당, 양도, 출구 중 하나가 필요한데 모두 제한적입니다. 배당은 매니저위원회의 절대적·단독 재량이라 보장이 없고 [A21], 현금의 5%는 배당 전에 계열사에 먼저 배정됩니다 [A20]. 양도는 1년 보유 제한 이후에도 위원회의 동의가 필요하고 매수자가 있다는 보장도 없습니다 [A24]. 공개시장은 없고 앞으로도 없을 가능성이 크며 발행사의 환매권도 없습니다 [A25]. 다만 동의 주체 설명이 쪽마다 다르다는 점은 유의해야 합니다. 둘째, 투자자는 10년간 취소 불가능한 의결권 위임을 하고 [A23], 위원회가 한도 없이 추가 Unit을 발행할 수 있다고 Form C가 설명하며 희석 방지 권리도 없습니다 [A26]. 다만 승인된 총 Unit이 1,000만 개로 적혀 있어 "무제한"은 다소 과장일 수 있습니다 [B6]. 창립 구성원이 완전희석 지분의 65%를 가지고 [A27], 정보·열람권도 법이 요구하는 범위로 제한됩니다 [B4].

가격은 Unit당 0.35달러이며 "임의로 정했다"고 공시되었으나 이것이 고평가의 증거는 아닙니다 [A3, A34]. 단순 산술로 발행 Unit 750만 개 기준 약 262만 5천 달러, 최대 모집 후 약 330만 5천 달러입니다 [K1, K3]. 이는 평가의견이 아닌 계산일 뿐입니다. 시드 SAFE 조건이 없어 완전희석 값은 계산하지 못했습니다 [K4].

부족한 정보: 매출은 0달러이고 정식 매출 활동이 시작되지 않았으며 [A13], 고객·계약·이용 데이터가 없습니다. 재무제표는 2026-04-30 기준 검토(비감사) 자료로 약 5.5개월 지났고 [A12], 6월 30일 현금과 24~36개월 런웨이는 검토받지 않은 발행인 주장입니다 [A14]. XML의 현금 0.00 표기 [A16], 부채 0 대 대출 언급 [C10], "자원 충분" 대 "자금 필수" 문구 [A19, B5]도 정리되지 않았습니다. 경쟁사, 경영진 이력, 사업 설명 섹션은 처리되지 않았고, 확인된 것은 CTO에 대한 2023년 CFTC 동의명령 공시뿐입니다 [A28, B7].

결론을 바꿀 수 있는 자료: 배당 정책 확약, 양도 동의 기준 완화, 청산 이벤트 정의와 출구 계획, 희석 한도 및 위임 범위 축소 등 계약 조건의 변화, 그리고 이후 기간의 재무자료와 매출·고객 실적, 시드 SAFE 조건이 있습니다.
